candidates.tagline: Singapore Airlines new biz class looks like Scoot, their own budget airline
candidates.story: On November 6, 2026, Singapore Airlines unveiled its new Boeing 777-9 Business Class designed by BMW Designworks — but the cabin's yellow-accented, dark gray palette looked so much like the finishes on Scoot (SIA's low-cost subsidiary) that aviation bloggers immediately nicknamed it 'Scoot J,' with one reviewer saying it looks like 'Scoot and Spirit Airlines had a baby.'
candidates.why_funny: One of the world's most prestigious airlines spent years developing a new Business Class and ended up with something indistinguishable from its own budget carrier.
candidates.alt: New Singapore Airlines Boeing 777-9 Business Class center seats showing gray and black upholstery with yellow accent stripes — a design critics immediately compared to Scoot's low-cost cabin aesthetic
candidates.credit: One Mile at a Time / Singapore Airlines
candidates.license: editorial — © Singapore Airlines / One Mile at a Time

candidates.tagline: Paid $200 for Logic Pro — Apple's new AI feature is subscription-only
candidates.story: On November 5, 2026, Apple released Logic Pro 13.0 with an AI-powered 'Intelligent Assistant' — but the feature requires a $12.99/month Apple Creator Studio subscription and is excluded from the $199.99 one-time-purchase version, reversing Apple's earlier promise that Logic Pro features would be identical regardless of which way you paid.
candidates.why_funny: Apple spent years mocking Adobe's subscription-only model, then launched their AI feature in their flagship paid DAW locked behind — a subscription.
candidates.alt: Screenshot of the Logic Pro 13 Intelligent Assistant AI feature panel with a subscription paywall notice, displayed against the Logic Pro DAW interface
